sections.skill: Tell extracting from interpreting and check each

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: Which request is extraction?

choices.text: "List every date mentioned in this contract."
"What does this clause really mean for me?"
"Is this contract fair to me, and should I sign it before the deadline next week?"

questions.correct_answer: "List every date mentioned in this contract."
questions.intro: With an uploaded document, two kinds of request are worth keeping apart. EXTRACTING pulls out what the document actually says: "List every date in this contract," "What is the total on this invoice?" INTERPRETING asks what it means or implies: "Is this contract fair?" "Should I sign?" Extraction can be checked directly against the document. Interpretation involves judgment, context the tool may not have, and sometimes expertise such as legal or medical knowledge. Use the tool to extract and organize, check the extraction, and treat interpretation as a starting point for your own judgment or a qualified person's.

sections.skill: Compare reading a thermometer with deciding if you are sick

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: Reading the number on a thermometer is...
questions.intro: Reading a THERMOMETER is extraction: it says 38.2 degrees, and anyone can check the number. Deciding "Am I sick enough to stay home or see a doctor?" is interpretation: it depends on other symptoms, your history and sometimes a doctor's judgment. A tool reading a document is similar. Pulling out what the page says is like reading the thermometer. Deciding what it means for you is like deciding whether you are sick.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Catch hidden extraction errors and disguised interpretation

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: A table of "all payments" from a 3-page statement skips one row that crossed a page break. What kind of error?

choices.text: An interpretation error, because the tool decided that row did not matter to the reader
No error; page breaks never matter

questions.intro: Extraction errors are easy to miss when the output looks tidy. A table of "all payments" may skip a row that spans two pages, misread a smudged number, or confuse similar fields such as "due date" and "invoice date." Interpretation can also hide in extraction requests: "List the risks in this contract" mixes the two, because deciding what counts as a risk is judgment. When accuracy matters, spot-check extracted items against the document, especially numbers, names and dates.
